$comment: The one default Rezz template, as numbers — the single source both sides read.
`services/docsvc/app/template_render.py` draws every download from these values and
`src/lib/tailor/template-metrics.ts` previews from them, so the Result screen shows the
document the user is about to get rather than a lookalike of it. The two used to hold
their own hand-kept copies (plus a third in the renderer's tests) with nothing to catch
drift; that is why the preview's headings ended up smaller than its own body text and
its bullets sat 29% looser than the PDF's. One file now, read by both.
Points, because points are what the renderer works in.
Layout rules encoded here, and why (researched 29 Sep 2026 against how Workday, iCIMS,
Greenhouse, Taleo, Sovren and Daxtra actually read a resume — they are text extractors
that segment on section headings, not scorers):
- A4 with a 40pt (0.55in) margin, inside the 0.5-1in band every guide agrees on.
- Single column. No tables, no text boxes, no photo, no icons, no skill bars.
- Contact details are body text, never a PDF header region — Workday and iCIMS strip
header/footer regions before parsing, so a name placed there disappears.
- `heading` outranks `bullet` in size. They were both 10.5 until 29 Sep 2026, which
left weight, caps and a rule as the only things separating a section from its body.
- A job header is two lines: `role` (employer, location, dates, bold) then
`job_title` (italic).
- Body text never below 10pt.
Re-cut 29 Sep 2026 against the owner's ATS-safe LaTeX reference (a Jake's-resume
variant): centered Huge bold name over a centered ink contact line, 14pt bold caps
headings with a solid ink rule tucked under (the faint gray hairline was one of the
generated-template tells), italic job titles, tighter margins and vertical rhythm.
`align` and `italic` per kind are read by both renderers.
Colours are the preview's, chosen on the canvas; the renderer converts to its 0-1
tuples.
$typeComment: Per block kind, the things the renderer decides:
size    — the font size it draws at.
leading — how far its y-cursor advances, which is the block's own height and
therefore the CSS `line-height` that reproduces it.
before/after — the `space()` it adds around the block, which is the CSS margin.
indent  — how far a bullet's text is pushed off the margin, dot drawn at the margin.
align   — center, for the header block; everything else is left.
italic  — the job title, per the reference's \textit second line.
A kind without `before`/`after` gets none: a `job_title` sits straight under its role,
and the next bullet straight under that.
